name: Marie Curie
bio: Marie Skłodowska Curie was a pioneer in radioactivity research and the first person awarded two Nobel Prizes.
contribution: Discovered radioactivity, isolated polonium and radium, and developed techniques for measuring radioactivity.

name: Albert Einstein
bio: Theoretical physicist who developed the theories of special and general relativity.
contribution: Theory of relativity, mass-energy equivalence (E=mc^2), contributions to quantum theory.

name: C. V. Raman
bio: Indian physicist known for the Raman effect in light scattering.
contribution: Discovery of the Raman effect, which provided insight into light-matter interactions.

name: Emmy Noether
bio: Mathematician whose theorem established the connection between symmetries and conservation laws in physics.
contribution: Noether's theorem linking symmetries and conservation laws, foundational for modern theoretical physics.

name: Léon Foucault
bio: French physicist and astronomer whose precision experiments made the motion of Earth visible.
contribution: His Foucault pendulum demonstrated Earth's rotation, and the Foucault knife-edge test measured the quality of telescope mirrors.

name: James Dewar
bio: Scottish physicist and chemist known for pioneering work in low-temperature physics.
contribution: He liquefied hydrogen and invented the vacuum flask, now commonly called a thermos, for thermal insulation.

name: Michael Faraday
bio: English scientist whose experiments established many of the foundations of modern electromagnetism.
contribution: His discoveries of electromagnetic induction, the laws of electrolysis, and diamagnetism shaped electric motors and generators.
